meta.headline: Talk to Atlas the way you would to a capable assistant who has read all your notes.
meta.title: Atlas Guide

intro: Talk to Atlas in your Atlas project the way you would to a capable assistant who has read all your notes. You never need to manage files or settings; just ask.

items: Nine pages that keep themselves up to date, including this guide.
Three automation profiles matched to your Claude plan.

sections.title: What Atlas does
sections.intro: Atlas remembers your work, keeps it organized, and moves it forward, without you asking each time.

items.title: Daily Brief
body: Every morning: today's meetings with prep notes, what's due or slipping, what changed overnight, who you're waiting on, and your top priorities.

items.title: Remembers everything you've told it
body: Ask about any decision, promise, person, or project. Atlas answers with where the information came from.
examples: What did we decide about enterprise pricing, and why?
What have I promised Jordan this month?

items.title: Writes in your voice
body: Emails, documents, decks, and status updates, grounded in what Atlas knows and written the way you write. Atlas never sends anything without your OK.
examples: Draft my pricing feedback for Jordan
Turn this week's progress into a status update

sections.title: What runs on its own
sections.intro: Automations run on a schedule that fits your Claude plan. See them in the Control Center.

items.title: Bring in new information
body: Reads new email, meetings, messages, and files you drop in Atlas Drop, and files what matters.

items.title: Draft emails
body: Drafts replies and follow-ups and leaves them in your drafts folder. Sending is always up to you.

items.title: Pause or reschedule anything
body: Every automation can be paused, moved, or switched off in plain language.
examples: Pause the weekly review while I'm on vacation

items.title: Forget something
body: Atlas can forget a record and stop collecting it. It always confirms first, and explains what stays in history.
examples: Forget everything about the Harbor side project

sections.title: If something looks wrong
sections.intro: Most problems are a connection that needs signing in again.

items.title: A connection expired
body: The Control Center shows which tool needs attention.
steps: In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors.
Find the tool marked as disconnected and choose Connect.
Come back to your Atlas project and say "I reconnected Outlook".

items.title: My brief looks out of date
body: If the nightly run was skipped, Atlas catches up the first time you open a chat. You can also ask directly.
examples: Why didn't last night's run work?
